text: On Millikan's teleosemantic theory, what fixes the content of a mental representation is:
choices: Whatever currently causes tokens of it under ideal conditions
Its inferential role within the subject's web of beliefs
The Shannon information it carries during a calibration period
Its biological proper function - what it was selected (in the organism's evolutionary history) to do
explanation: Teleosemantics (Millikan, in Language, Thought, and Other Biological Categories, 1984) fixes content by a representation's biological proper function - what it was selected to do in the organism's evolutionary history - which lets it handle misrepresentation naturally as failure to perform that function. Option 0 is pure causal covariance, option 2 is Dretske's informational account, and option 1 is inferential-role semantics; each is a distinct rival theory of content.
